messages:
elena: heads up — found a mismatch between the Console role matrix and the policy service for the `editor` role on project-scoped resources. UI shows editor can rotate KMS keys but backend denies.

michael: omg ok, how did you spot it?

elena: customer reported a '403' when trying to rotate a key from the Console. I traced it: UI sends action=rotate_key, console-frontend maps role->perm as `key.rotate`, but the policy service expects `kms:rotate_key` under `project:{id}`. mapping drift.

kyle: can you paste the request/policy check log?

elena: sure — from audit logs: 
```
ts=2025-10-12T16:02:13Z svc=console req_id=8f2a user=acct:dana@example.com role=editor action=kms:RotateKey resource=project:acme:key/xyz result=DENY reason=policy_mismatch
```

pri: notable — we recently refactored the role matrix to collapse org vs project perms. maybe a mapping table didn't get updated.

michael: do we have a simple repro? can I repro in staging?

elena: yes — I repro'd in staging. steps: 1) login as editor@staging 2) UI -> Keys -> rotate -> click confirm -> 403. backend logs the same mismatch.

kyle: probable cause: frontend still uses legacy permission name `key.rotate` in the request context when calling the policy check middleware. the policy service now normalizes to `kms:RotateKey`. small mapping bug.

michael: quick mitigation: gate the UI button so only admin shows rotate until fix? or fallback to ask-for-access flow?

elena: we should avoid removing editor UX broadly. prefer patching the frontend mapping and adding a compatibility alias in policy service. low blast radius.

pri: agreed. timeline?

kyle: I can do a frontend patch + unit test. add a compatibility rule in policy service for one week. I’ll open PRs.

michael: also add an audit rule to flag mismatched-perm denies so we catch similar regressions early. audit-bot: can you create a saved query?

audit-bot: created saved query "rbac:mismatch-deny" -> /audit/queries/3752 (auto-added alert for >5 denies/hour)

elena: thanks. also saw a secondary issue: when editor was denied for rotate, the UI still showed the success toast and left the spinner on. that's a UX bug — confusing.

kyle: ugh. I’ll fix both: the perm mapping and the toast handling. estimated PRs by end of day.

michael: deploy plan? patch -> canary -> full?

kyle: patch frontend + compatibility alias in policy service, canary on staging -> prod canary (10%) -> monitor audit query & error rates -> full rollout.

pri: add regression test in console e2e: simulate editor rotate and assert deny vs allow based on mapping.

elena: I'll post the minimal repro steps + logs in the ticket.

michael: also check logs for KMS encrypt/decrypt operations — if mapping drifted there we might have latent denies.

elena: scanned last 24h: only rotate showed denies from this drift. encrypt/decrypt fine.

michael: ok. can we avoid adding a long-lived compatibility alias? only keep for 7 days and then enforce strict names.

kyle: yes, alias TTL=7d. I'll include in policy service PR.

pri: assign to kyle, reviewers elena+michael. please include release notes and a short blurb for incident postmortem channel.

kyle: assigning now. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/console/+/2345

michael: thanks. one last ask — let's add an automated check in CI to validate frontend permission strings against the canonical policy manifest on each build. would have caught this.

\eli{elena}: totally. I can add a small linter that fails build if mapping has unknown perms.

kyle: will queue that after fix.

\deploy-bot: staged deploy started for console-frontend v2.14.3-canary (10%): deploy_id=deploy-6623

elena: monitoring audit query, will update when denies stop. :eyes:

michael: thanks team. please ping #incidents if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
